newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada April industrial price index rises 0.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Canada April industrial price index rises 0.5 pct.

text.p: Statistics Canada on Wednesday issued the following economic indicators for April.
INDUSTRIAL PRODUCT PRICE INDEX Month-on-Month Year-on-Year
INDUSTRIAL PRODUCT PRICE INDEX Month-on-Month Year-on-Year
The IPPI reflects the prices producers receive as goods leave their plants.
A Reuters survey of economists had forecast that the overall index would rise 0.2 percent in April from March.

Statistics Canada said that most of the 0.5 percent rise in the month was linked to the value of the U.S. dollar on export prices quoted in U.S. currency. Excluding the effect of the currency, there would be almost no change in the price level for the seventh consecutive month.
The currency impact was most noticeable for motor vehicles, pulp, paper and wood products, StatsCan said.
The only notable decline for the month was petroleum products.
The federal agency said the increase in the 12-month change in prices was due more to declining prices from last December to April than to rising prices in early 1997.
